turns.speaker: Case manager
turns.text: Okay so we're recording, you good with that?

turns.speaker: Client
turns.text: Yeah that's fine.

turns.speaker: Case manager
turns.text: Alright, so tell me your name for the file.

turns.speaker: Client
turns.text: Darius Johnson. D-A-R-I-U-S.

turns.speaker: Case manager
turns.text: And how old are you Darius?

turns.speaker: Client
turns.text: Forty one. I'll be forty two in March.

turns.speaker: Case manager
turns.text: Where are you staying right now?

turns.speaker: Client
turns.text: I'm at my sister's in Inglewood, off 63rd and Halsted, on her couch. She said I can stay till the end of the month but after that I don't know.

turns.speaker: Case manager
turns.text: Okay. When did you come home?

turns.speaker: Client
turns.text: Last Thursday. I came out of Stateville, did six years.

turns.speaker: Case manager
turns.text: And you're on MSR?

turns.speaker: Client
turns.text: Yeah, two years MSR, my parole agent is a Miss Ortiz, I see her the 19th.

turns.speaker: Case manager
turns.text: What's the best number for you?

turns.speaker: Client
turns.text: 773 555 0148. That's my sister's phone though, I ain't got one yet.

turns.speaker: Case manager
turns.text: What about ID, you got your state ID?

turns.speaker: Client
turns.text: No, they gave me the release papers and that's it, I lost my old ID before I went in.

turns.speaker: Case manager
turns.text: Okay, I'm going to take you to the Secretary of State on King Drive Friday morning, we'll get that started.

turns.speaker: Case manager
turns.text: And medical?

turns.speaker: Client
turns.text: I'm on blood pressure pills, they gave me like ten days worth.

turns.speaker: Case manager
turns.text: You got a doctor?

turns.speaker: Client
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: Case manager
turns.text: Okay we need to get you on Medicaid then.

turns.speaker: Case manager
turns.text: Work?

turns.speaker: Client
turns.text: I got my forklift certificate inside, I want to get on at a warehouse.

turns.speaker: Case manager
turns.text: Okay, we'll talk about that once the ID's done.

turns.speaker: Client
turns.text: Alright.

turns.speaker: Case manager
turns.text: Anything else?

turns.speaker: Client
turns.text: Nah that's it for now.

key_info.comment: This is his sister's phone; he does not have his own yet.

key_info.heard_as: I'll be forty two in March
key_info.comment: Only the month was given: he turns 42 in March, so likely born March 1985, day not said.
Client said two years MSR (mandatory supervised release), Illinois's form of parole.

immediate_needs.detail: About ten days of blood pressure pills from release, running out soon; no doctor
No state ID; only release papers
On sister's couch until end of month, nothing after
Wants warehouse work; has forklift certificate

next_steps.action: Take client to Secretary of State on King Drive to start state ID
Talk about warehouse job search once ID is done
Report to parole agent Miss Ortiz
Find a doctor or clinic to refill blood pressure pills before they run out
Start looking for housing for after the end of the month
Help client apply for a Lifeline phone
